sources.title: National Museum of China: bronze sword of King Fuchai of Wu
sources.note: Direct Chinese museum text checked. Object description, Fuchai accession in 495 BCE, defeat of Yue the following year, Huangchi in 482 and conquest in 473. Traditional Taibo genealogy is not used to validate the imported 1500 BCE start.

sources.title: National Museum of China: bronze jian of King Fuchai
sources.note: Direct Chinese text checked. Jian vessel functions are generic possibilities, not a proven biography of this particular object. English parallel gives dimensions and weight, but is not needed for the public claims.

sources.title: National Museum of China: Cai Hou Shen zun
sources.note: Direct Chinese text checked: 518 BCE bridal vessel for Da Meng Ji, Cai-Wu marriage, and 1955 Shouxian discovery. Cai material is explicitly comparative evidence for an alliance, not a Wu tomb.

sources.title: Wang, Chen, Zhang, Zhang and Wu: The history of agriculture in the mountainous areas of the lower Yangtze River since the late Neolithic (2022)
sources.note: Primary publisher indexed abstract and Tables 1-2 checked with exact DOI query. Direct newer PDF endpoint refuses download. Later agricultural layer is 2667-2568 calibrated years BP, roughly eighth to seventh centuries BCE; table gives 44 rice and 92 foxtail millet remains. No political affiliation inferred from crops.

sources.title: Suzhou Local Chronicles Office: competing identifications of Helu city
sources.note: Direct Chinese article read. Contains conflicting proposed capital identifications and some inconsistent Yancheng measurements; public draft uses only clearly described Mudu walls, water gate, stone road, workshops, pottery and explicit unresolved capital identity.

sources.title: Zhou Jianlin: rescue restoration and conservation of the Spring and Autumn dugout canoe from Yancheng, Wujin
sources.note: Primary conservator paper hosted by Chinese Association for Conservation Technology of Cultural Heritage. Direct PDF text is garbled; indexed original first-page text readable using exact Chinese title. Introduction gives 1965 discovery, 7.45 m length, nanmu timber and severe cracking/shrinkage; no oldest-boat superlative used.

sources.title: Wujin Museum: second expert review of the Yancheng canoe conservation plan (2020)
sources.note: Direct institutional indexed text checked: September 28-29 meeting, prior 3-D modelling and condition assessment, preventive conservation discussed. Future plan is not described as completed restoration.

sources.title: Benjamin Daniels, Wu Yue Scripts: Wu inscriptions
sources.note: Direct scholarly corpus checked. Fuchai spear section cites Jicheng 18.11534, Dong Chuping 1992 pp.133-134, Shi Xiejie 1998 p.552 and Dong Shan 2014 no.51. All transcriptions begin 吳王夫差. Heading supplies English identification. About page identifies author as UC Berkeley history PhD candidate and first-hand examination at Hubei Provincial Museum.

sources.title: Benjamin Daniels, Wu Yue Scripts: chronological catalogue
sources.note: Direct scholarly catalogue checked: Shoumeng 585-561 BCE, Guang/Helu 514-496 BCE, later weapons to 473 BCE. Dates delimit the catalogue, not proof of an exact founding date.

sources.title: Hubei Provincial Museum: Spear of Fuchai
sources.note: Direct English museum record checked: late Spring and Autumn, length 29.5 cm, unearthed from Mashan No.5 tomb in Jiangling in 1983. Inscription transcription checked separately in the scholarly corpus.

sources.title: Wang Yangfan: Grand Canal cultural corridor, Instituto Confucio magazine 2024 no.1
sources.note: Direct institutional bilingual PDF, printed page 6: Fuchai ordered Han Gou between Yangzhou and Huaian in 486 BCE; later Sui, Yuan, Ming and Qing expansion. Hosted by Shanghai International Studies University; published by Chinese International Education Foundation.

proposedOverrides.name: Wu
proposedOverrides.summary: The lower-Yangtze kingdom of Wu, its royal bronzes, regional farming and final struggle with Yue, with imported dates distinguished from documented history.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Only this exact indexed ID is covered; no aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: Index explicitly links Wu (state). Three reused lower-Yangtze polygons in world-bc1500, world-bc1000 and world-bc700 have bounds 116.6717667176672 to 121.77301773017729 E and 27.849407137651838 to 34.69127435843281 N. They are not evidence of fixed frontiers throughout 1500-500 BCE.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Earliest imported date is not treated as a historical founding. Periods begin with regional archaeological context in the eighth century; the final period explicitly continues beyond the imported cutoff through the historical 473 BCE conquest. Override retains map_coverage and no invented fall date.
batchIdentityNotes.overlap: Exact index/override/card/staged check found no Eastern Wu, Southern Wu or Wuyue association to share. Unrelated IDs containing the letters wu in American/Oceanian names are false-positive string matches only.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Jingshuidun is regional subsistence evidence, not a proved politically Wu village. Cai marriage vessel is explicitly Cai provenance. Mudu capital identification is unresolved. No supported school, medical or sanitation system was located; none is invented.
